headline: Highest risk is medium: Airflow’s broad egress plus RisingWave’s shared data-engineering role create plausible leakage and cascading-error paths, while prompt-injection and compliance risks are not evidenced.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No shared communication channel is documented. Airflow shows broad network egress, but RisingWave has network egress none and neither profile shows clipboard, shared filesystem, or MCP bridging. With only docs-level evidence, a prompt-injection pathway is not established.
conditions: IF both agents are connected through a shared filesystem, clipboard, or message queue not shown in the profiles, reassess upward.
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces.
Disable any manual copy-paste bridge for untrusted content.
Add provenance labels to any exchanged text.
requires-engineering: introduce a trusted message broker with content tagging.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Airflow has broad network egress, so if it is given sensitive files or secrets it can transmit them outward; RisingWave shows no egress and no touched data classes. The pair lacks evidence of shared storage or sensitive data, so leakage is plausible but not demonstrated beyond a small, configuration-dependent blast radius.
conditions: IF either agent is pointed at a shared workspace containing secrets or regulated data, leakage risk increases.
IF Airflow tasks are configured to read and forward file contents, reassess upward.
mitigations: Restrict Airflow DAGs to non-sensitive inputs.
Store secrets outside any shared directory.
Review outbound destinations for Airflow.
Use separate service accounts for each agent.
requires-engineering: add egress allowlisting and DLP scanning.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents are data-engineering systems, but the profiles do not show overlapping write surfaces, shared mutable resources, or locking gaps. Airflow’s broad egress and RisingWave’s no-egress posture reduce direct write contention evidence; any conflict would require an unshown shared target such as a filesystem or database.
conditions: IF both agents are later granted write access to the same directory or database, reassess upward.
IF an orchestrator places them on a shared mutable resource without locks, conflict becomes material.
mitigations: Assign distinct output directories.
Avoid concurrent writes to the same tables.
Serialize any shared updates.
Check for hidden shared mounts before deployment.
requires-engineering: add optimistic locking around shared state.

D_cascading_error.rationale: A plausible pipeline exists where Airflow produces outputs that RisingWave consumes, but neither profile shows verification or provenance checks. Because both are data-engineering tools, the interaction is more than hypothetical, and unverified handoff can propagate bad facts or malformed jobs into downstream work products.
conditions: IF Airflow output is fed into RisingWave without validation, cascading errors are likely.
IF RisingWave treats upstream artifacts as authoritative, impact expands to downstream datasets or views.
mitigations: Insert schema validation between agents.
Require human review for generated SQL or DAG changes.
Compare outputs against a known-good checksum.
Log and diff upstream artifacts before execution.
requires-engineering: add automated provenance and contract checks.

E_compliance.rationale: No residency, certification, retention, or regulated data handling mismatch is evidenced. Both profiles are docs-only, touch no data classes, and provide no compliance-specific surfaces; therefore a compliance breach pathway is not supported by the available evidence.
conditions: IF either agent is later assigned regulated data or a residency-constrained deployment, reassess compliance risk.
mitigations: Document data-class handling before deployment.
Keep regulated data out of both agents until reviewed.
Add a retention policy check.
requires-engineering: map each agent to a formal compliance control set.
